analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. It modifies docs/provider/cli-reference.md by adding one bullet (head lines 1020-1031) to the `darkbloom status` output description. The bullet documents a 'Requests served since the daemon started' line: a per-daemon count of finished coordinator requests, with output token totals only. It notes that the count resets on daemon restart or when a scheduled availability window opens. It includes requests ended early by cancel or dropped connection, and free self-route requests. It points to coordinator/registry/heartbeat.go `cumulativeDelta` (an immutable platform link) and `StatusCommand+ServedRequests.swift`. Both units were reviewed. They are base-side context around the change (the status section and the surrounding CLI reference) and contain no changed lines.

Security relevance: the added text describes a local operator-visible counter. It exposes no prompt content (A-001), keys, tokens or attestation data, and changes no trust boundary or authorization behavior. The counter is provider self-reported, and the text correctly says the coordinator may not pay for early-ended requests and that paid earnings are on the console. This is consistent with the model that providers are adversarial, so the counter is not a billing authority (ADV-001; T-007 context). No code, config, endpoint or deployment change is made, so no existing threat assumption is invalidated.

Limits: the underlying StatusCommand+ServedRequests.swift and the referenced coordinator heartbeat.go are not in the supplied evidence. I cannot verify that the described behavior matches the implementation, for example whether the counter leaks anything beyond counts. That is a documentation-accuracy question, not a demonstrated security issue. No threat-model update is needed.
